newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hopewell unit to bid for Philippine gas project.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell unit to bid for Philippine gas project.

text.p: A unit of Hong Kong's Hopewell Holdings Ltd has said it was all set to submit its tender to build a 1,200-megawatt Philippine gas-fired power plant at a rebidding on Monday for the controversial project. "We are participating in the rebidding. Definitely we are showing up on Monday," Edgardo Bautista, executive director of Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (Cepa), told reporters at the weekend.

Cepa submitted the lowest bid at the original bidding last year. But state-owned National Power Corp (Napocor) declared the bidding a failure, alleging Cepa's partner, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd, had ties with Westinghouse Electric Corp of the United States.
Cepa and Mitsubishi denied the allegation, but Napocor decided there was need for a rebidding.
Besides Cepa, 19 local and foreign companies participated in a pre-bidding conference on the project in Ilijan, Batangas province, south of Manila.

The government had banned Westinghouse from local power projects in a row over a 620-megawatt nuclear power plant in nearby Bataan province. It lifted the ban last year after a $100 million compromise agreement.
